Q: How to get the file path for a file in google drive for use in colab? A:

There is a lot simpler way with no extra coding

from google.colab import drive
drive.mount('/content/drive')

You have to use this command to mount the file inevitably. when the file is mounted in your collab notebook, just click on file tab which is on the right. browse to the desired file and click on three dots copy its file location. Its that simple.

Q: Accessing jasper reports through the web A:

The topic is old, but I’m leaving this note for anyone still looking for a lightweight way to view reports on the web.

You don't necessarily need JasperReports Server (which is a commerical product now) for rendering reports as html. You can fill the report and then export it as HTML through JasperReports Library APIs. Interactivity like drill downs and pagination requires some effort but for simple reports, you can embed images and charts and render the HTML in an iframe.

Basically using JasperFillManager for filling and JasperExportManager for exporting. Built-in HtmlExporter supports interactive vs static html. If you configured your report to embed the charts and images, you can use static html output. If you need page links or other links that you want to capture through JavaScript, you need interactive exports or you may output specific JS file of yours that would listen to click events in the iframe; though I'd prefer the interactive mode where JR Library captures link metadata and you generate your scripts based on that metadata. For most reports, static html is just fine.

After implementing this manually in several Spring Boot apps, we eventually bundled our logic into a reusable SDK/framework to save time. We've just made it available at reportshell.com. It’s a commercial tool, but it's free to use for development and evaluation. If you don't want to purchase it, I think the documentation may still help you implement a similar flow for your own needs. If it is just one app with simple reports and simple parameters, then you don't need any tool at all. JR Library is enough.

You may also check BIRT Viewer for how they use web APIs for similar stuff. Backend code is of course different but it helps on how to design a web api for report viewers.

Q: VBA placing date format dd/mm/yyyy as mm/dd/yyyy A:

This is how Excel handles the VBA instruction:

ActiveSheet.Range("K23").Value = Format(Now(), "dd/mm/yyyy")

The Format function returns a string variant data type to the cell as it is defined in the format expression. This is in the example 03/07/2023.
But there is a second process in Excel which is activated when the data is placed in the cell.
Only the part which involves the issue is, that if a cell content can be identified as a Date then Excel will display it in the format defined in Format Cells -> Number -> Category pane.
If it is General Excel will apply the actually defined format for Date.
In your case the local can be English (US) or the format explicitely set to mm/dd/yyyy which will displays the date in mm/dd/yyyy format.
When you remove the slashes the string cannot be identified as a date and so Excel will leave it as it is.

ActiveSheet.Range("K23").Value = Format(Now(), "dd mm yyyy")
